title: Jaffna Kings Owners Terminated Mid-Season as LPL Corruption Scandal Deepens
excerpt: Sri Lanka Cricket and tournament operator IPG have seized control of the four-time champions after co-owner Manjot Kalra's arrest on match-fixing charges and the franchise's failure to meet financial obligations.
body:
• Sri Lanka Cricket and tournament operator IPG have terminated Sports Commune's franchise agreement with the Jaffna Kings mid-season, citing the owners' inability to meet financial obligations.
  • Co-owner Manjot Kalra, a former India Under-19 World Cup hero, was arrested on LPL 2026's opening day on allegations of offering over US$30,000 to players to fix matches. He has been remanded until July 31.
  • The other co-owner, entrepreneur Mayank Goel, has reportedly gone missing since the arrest.
  • SLC and IPG have assumed full control; the Bhanuka Rajapaksa-led squad will continue competing without changes to the roster or fixtures.

Sri Lanka Cricket and tournament rights holder Innovative Production Group terminated the franchise agreement with the Jaffna Kings' ownership group on Thursday, stripping Sports Commune of its stake in one of the Lanka Premier League's most decorated teams just one week into the tournament's sixth edition.

The termination follows the arrest of co-owner Manjot Kalra on the opening day of LPL 2026, July 17, and what organisers described as the franchisee's "inability to fulfil its financial obligations." All rights to the Jaffna Kings have reverted to IPG, which will run the team jointly with SLC for the remainder of the season.

The Arrest That Sparked the Crisis

Kalra, a former India Under-19 cricketer best known for his unbeaten century in India's 2018 Under-19 World Cup final triumph, was detained by Sri Lanka Police's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) for the Prevention of Offences Relating to Sports just hours before the LPL's opening match at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo.

According to court proceedings reported by Cricbuzz, police told a Colombo magistrate that Kalra had allegedly approached three Sri Lankan internationals — Bhanuka Rajapaksa, Dunith Wellalage, and Avishka Fernando, all members of the Kings squad — and offered sums exceeding US$30,000 to influence match results. Investigators said the players possessed voice recordings and video evidence, and that the approach had been reported approximately 10 days before the arrest.

Kalra was remanded in custody until July 31, with bail denied to preserve the investigation. His defence team has denied all allegations.

"Having had the privilege of representing India with honour, Mr. Kalra fully understands the responsibility and integrity expected of those associated with Indian sport. He remains confident that the truth will prevail."

— Statement from Manjot Kalra's legal representatives

Ownership Collapse

Sports Commune, the sports management company that acquired the Jaffna Kings in May 2026, was led by Kalra alongside entrepreneur Mayank Goel, founder of Softsecure Infotech and Shree Dhyan Insurance Brokers. With Kalra behind bars, Cricbuzz reported that the other co-owner had "vanished," leaving the franchise rudderless. IPG and SLC stepped in to guarantee continuity, assuming responsibility for all player and staff contracts.

"While this was a difficult decision, our priority has always been to protect the integrity of the Lanka Premier League and ensure complete stability for our players, coaches, partners, and fans."

— Anil Mohan, CEO, IPG

On the Field, Kings Carry On

Despite the turmoil, Jaffna Kings have won two of their first three matches under captain Bhanuka Rajapaksa. Pre-draft signings including Bangladesh stars Shakib Al Hasan and Taskin Ahmed have bolstered a competitive squad coached by former Sri Lankan skipper Thilina Kandamby. Organisers confirmed no changes to the squad, format, or fixtures. The tournament is scheduled to conclude on August 8 at the R. Premadasa Stadium.

A Recurring Pattern

The Jaffna Kings franchise has endured serial ownership instability. Winners of the inaugural LPL in 2020, the team was terminated by SLC in 2021 over financial issues before being revived under Lyca Group. That arrangement also collapsed ahead of the 2025 season. Sports Commune's tenure lasted barely two months.

For Kalra, the arrest adds to a troubled trajectory. His promising cricket career was cut short years ago by an age-fraud controversy, according to Cricket Addictor. His pivot to sports business has now ended in a Sri Lankan jail cell.

Anti-Corruption Laws in Focus

The case is an early test for Sri Lanka's Prevention of Offences Related to Sports law, enacted in 2019, which made Sri Lanka the first South Asian nation to criminalise match-fixing. Convictions carry prison sentences of up to 10 years.

"Sri Lanka Cricket has a zero-tolerance approach to corruption and unethical practices," SLC said in a statement. The episode also highlights due diligence risks in franchise cricket at a time when several LPL teams have changed hands to new Indian-origin investor groups this season — transitions that, until now, had been smooth.
nri_angle: Indian entrepreneurs Manjot Kalra and Mayank Goel, who owned the franchise through Sports Commune, face corruption allegations in Sri Lankan cricket, highlighting the risks for Indian-origin investors in international franchise leagues.
